events.title: George Washington Is Inaugurated as First U.S. President
events.description: On a balcony of Federal Hall in New York City, George Washington took the oath of office. He became the first president of the United States under the new Constitution.
events.significance: The ceremony set many precedents for the American presidency and marked the start of the federal government as we know it.

events.title: The Louisiana Purchase Agreement Is Concluded
events.description: The United States agreed to buy the Louisiana Territory from France. The deal covered a vast stretch of land west of the Mississippi River.
events.significance: The purchase roughly doubled the size of the young nation and opened the way for westward expansion.

events.title: Adolf Hitler Dies in His Berlin Bunker
events.description: As Soviet forces closed in on Berlin, Adolf Hitler took his own life in the Führerbunker. His death came one day after his marriage to Eva Braun. Soviet troops raised their flag over the Reichstag the same day.
events.significance: His death brought the Nazi regime close to collapse. Germany's surrender followed within days, ending the war in Europe.

events.title: The Fall of Saigon
events.description: North Vietnamese forces took Saigon, the capital of South Vietnam, and the South Vietnamese government surrendered. The city was soon renamed Ho Chi Minh City.
events.significance: The fall effectively ended the Vietnam War and led to the reunification of Vietnam. The date is now marked there as Reunification Day.
